Commentary of al-Tha'alabi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 60, verses 1–11 (part 1 of 2):

Medinan. It has one thousand five hundred and ten letters, three hundred and forty-eight words, and thirteen verses.

Al-Jabbari related to us, saying: Ibn Hayyan related to us, saying: al-Furqadi related to us, saying: Isma'il ibn 'Amr related to us, saying: Yusuf ibn 'Atiyyah related to us, saying: Harun ibn Kathir related to us, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam related to us, from his father, from Abu Umamah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever recites Surat al-Mumtahanah, the believing men and women will be his intercessors on the Day of Resurrection." [270] [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/443.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies...﴾

It was revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, and the reason was that Sarah, a freedwoman of Abu 'Amr ibn Sayfi ibn Hashim ibn 'Abd Manaf, came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from Makkah to Madinah two years after Badr, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was preparing for the conquest of Makkah. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to her: "Have you come as a Muslim?" She said: No. He said: "Have you come as an emigrant?" She said: No. He said: "Then what brought you?" She said: "You were the origin, the kin and the clients, and my clients have gone, and I have been struck by severe need, so I came to you that you might give me, clothe me and provide me with transport." He said to her: "Then where are you from the youths of Makkah?" [271] [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 18/51; Zad al-Masir: 8/2.]] — and she was a singer and a wailing woman.

She said: "Nothing was asked of me after the battle of Badr." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) urged the sons of 'Abd al-Muttalib and the sons of al-Muttalib concerning her, and they clothed her, provided her with transport and gave her provision. Then Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, an ally of the Banu Asad ibn 'Abd al-'Uzza, came to her, wrote a letter with her to the people of Makkah, and gave her ten dinars. This is the narration of Badhan from Ibn 'Abbas. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: he gave her ten dirhams. They said: and he clothed her in a cloak, so that she might deliver the letter to the people of Makkah. He wrote in the letter: "From Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah to the people of Makkah: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intends you, so take your precautions." Sarah set out, and Jibril descended and informed the Prophet (ﷺ) of what had been done. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent 'Ali, 'Ammar, 'Umar, al-Zubayr, Talhah, al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad and Abu Murthad, and they were all horsemen. He said to them:

"Set out until you reach Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman traveling with a letter from Hatib to the polytheists. Take it from her and let her go her way. If she does not hand it over to you, then strike her neck."

They set out until they overtook her at the very place the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had described. They said to her: "Where is the letter?" She swore by Allah that she had no letter with her. They searched her and went through her belongings, but found no letter with her, and they were about to return. 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "By Allah, we have not lied, nor have we been lied to," and he drew his sword and said: "Bring out the letter, or by Allah I will strip you and strike your neck!" When she saw their determination, she brought out from her braid the letter she had hidden in her hair. They let her go her way, did not stop her or those with her, and returned with the letter to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for Hatib, and he came to him. He said to him: "Do you recognize this letter?" He said: "Yes." He said: "What moved you to do what you did?"

He said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I have not disbelieved since I embraced Islam, nor have I deceived you since I gave you counsel, nor have I responded to them since I parted from them. But there was no one among the emigrants except that he had someone in Makkah who protects his kin, and I was a man of standing among them, and my family were among them. I feared for my family, so I wanted to gain a favor with them. I knew that Allah would send down His punishment upon them, and that my letter would not avail them anything." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) believed him and excused him. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, let me strike the neck of this hypocrite." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "What do you know, O 'Umar? Perhaps Allah has looked upon the people of Badr and said to them: 'Do whatever you wish, for I have forgiven you.'" [272] [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 28/75; Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/369.]]

Abdullah ibn Hamid related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ghalib related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad related to us, saying: Layth related to us, from Abu al-Dunayr, from Jabir, that a slave of Hatib came complaining about Hatib to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Hatib will surely enter the Fire!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "You have lied; he will never enter it, for he witnessed Badr and al-Hudaybiyah." [273] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 10/401, no. 29960.]]

Allah, glorified is He, revealed concerning the matter of Hatib and his correspondence with the polytheists: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, extending to them affection...﴾ — "extending to them affection": here "bi" (with) is extra (ṣilah), like the saying of a speaker: "I want to go" and "I want to go with" — Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation by wrongdoing﴾ [[Surat al-Hajj: 25.]], meaning deviation in wrongdoing. From this is the words of the poet:

"When she drank, he shook the staff for her, / a miser, at the drinking-place, a spoiler of the water"

meaning: she drank. [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 28/73.]]

﴿...while they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth, expelling the Messenger and you [from Makkah] because you believe in Allah, your Lord. If you have gone out to strive in My cause and seeking My approval...﴾ — "wa qad" (and indeed) is the particle of circumstance. The order of the verse involves inversion and reordering: "Do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, extending to them affection, while they have disbelieved in what has come to you... If you have gone out to strive in My cause and seeking My approval, [then] you secretly extend to them affection, and I am most knowing of what you conceal and what you declare. And whoever of you does that has strayed from the right way." ﴿If they overcome you﴾ — that is, they see you and prevail over you — ﴿they will be enemies to you and will extend against you their hands﴾ — with killing — ﴿and their tongues﴾ — with evil, that is, with reviling — ﴿and they wish that you would disbelieve.﴾ So do not give them counsel, for they will not give you counsel nor show you affection.

﴿Never will your relatives benefit you or your children on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ He says: Do not let your kinship and your children, who are in Makkah, lead you to betray the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers, to abandon giving them counsel, and to take their enemies as allies and support them. Your relatives and children, for whose sake you have disobeyed Allah, will not benefit you. ﴿He will separate you﴾ — so that the people of obedience and faith in Him enter Paradise, and the people of disobedience and disbelief in Him enter the Fire.

The reciters differed concerning His words ﴿yafsilu baynakum﴾ (He will separate between you). ʿĀṣim, Yaʿqub and Abu Hatim read it with a fatḥah on the yā' and a kasrah on the ṣād, lightened. Ḥamzah, al-Kisa'i and Khalaf read it with a ḍammah on the yā' and a kasrah on the ṣād, emphasized (shaddah). Ibn ʿĀmir and al-Aʿraj read it with a ḍammah on the yā', a fatḥah on the ṣād, and emphasized. Ṭalḥah and al-Nakha'i read it with the nūn and a kasrah on the ṣād with emphasis. Abu Ḥaywah read it as yufṣilu from afṣala, yufṣilu. The rest read it with a ḍammah on the yā' and a fatḥah on the ṣād, lightened, from al-faṣl (separation).

﴿And Allah is Seeing of what you do.﴾

Abdullah ibn Hamid related to us, saying: Makki related to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Hashim related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from 'Ata' ibn Yazid, from Tamim al-Dari, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Religion is sincere counsel" three times. They said: "To whom, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "To Allah, to His Book, to His Messenger, to the leaders of the Muslims and their common folk." [274] [[Kanz al-'Ummal: 3/412, no. 7197; Sunan al-Darimi: 2/311.]]

﴿There has already been for you an excellent example in Ibrahim and those with him, when they said to their people: "Indeed, we are free of you and of what you worship other than Allah. We have disbelieved in you, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in Allah alone"...﴾ — "an excellent example" means a good model. "Bura'a'" is the plural of "barī'," and the common reading follows the pattern fu'alā' without being declined. ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read it as bira'un with a kasrah on the bā', on the pattern of faʿāl, like qaṣīr and qiṣār, ṭawīl and ṭiwāl. ﴿We have disbelieved in you﴾ — that is, we have denied you and rejected your religion. ﴿...except for the saying of Ibrahim to his father: "I will surely ask forgiveness for you, though I have no power to obtain anything for you from Allah"...﴾ — meaning: there has been for you an excellent example in Ibrahim and his affairs, except in his saying to his father. They were forbidden to take Ibrahim as a model in this particular matter, so that they would seek forgiveness for the polytheists. Then He explained his excuse in Surat al-Tawbah.

In this verse there is clear evidence of the superiority of our Prophet (ﷺ), for when he was commanded to be followed, he was commanded absolutely without exception, saying: ﴿What the Messenger has given you, take; and what he has forbidden you, refrain from.﴾ But when they were commanded to follow Ibrahim, an exception was made.

﴿Our Lord, upon You we have relied, and to You we have turned, and to You is the final return. Our Lord, make us not a trial for the disbelievers and forgive us, our Lord; indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾ [This is the saying] [[The wording in the manuscript is obscured; the apparent reading is what we have recorded. In Tafsir al-Qurtubi (18/57): this is from the supplication of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and his companions.]] — of Ibrahim and those with him among the believers.

﴿There has already been for you in them an excellent example for whoever hopes for Allah and the Last Day. And whoever turns away — indeed, Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.﴾ — meaning in Ibrahim and those with him of the prophets and the friends of Allah. When this verse was revealed, the believers became hostile to their polytheist relatives for the sake of Allah and openly displayed enmity and disavowal toward them. Allah, glorified is He, knew the intensity of the believers' grief over this, so He revealed: ﴿Perhaps Allah will place affection between you, O believers, and those among them whom you have shown enmity — from the polytheists of Makkah. And Allah is All-Powerful, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ Allah does this by causing many of them to embrace Islam, so they became their allies and brothers, mixed with them, and intermarried with them.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married Umm Habibah bint Abi Sufyan ibn Harb — this is the one whom Abu Sufyan fathered. Umm Habibah had been married to 'Abdullah ibn Jahsh ibn Dhiyab, and she and her husband were among the emigrants to Abyssinia. He looked at her with desire and tried to win her to his religion, but she refused and remained steadfast in her religion, and her husband died as a Christian. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent to the Negus concerning her, to propose to her on his behalf. The Negus said to his companions: "Who has the best right to her?" They said: "Khalid ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As." He said: "Then marry her to your Prophet." He did so, and the Negus gave her dower as four hundred dinars and paid it to her himself. It is also said that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) proposed to 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, and when he gave her in marriage to him, he sent to the Negus concerning her; he (the Negus) paid the dower on his behalf and sent her to him. This reached Abu Sufyan, who was then a polytheist, and he said: "That is a stallion whose nose is not rubbed in the dust."

Allah, glorified is He, permitted kindness toward those who did not fight the believers and did not expel them, from among all the disbelievers. He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over the religion and do not expel you from your homes — from being righteous toward them and acting justly toward them. Indeed, Allah loves the just.﴾ — that is, deal justly with them with kindness and goodness. The scholars differed concerning those about whom this verse was revealed.

Ibn 'Abbas said: It was revealed concerning Khuza'ah, among them Hilal ibn 'Adiy, Khuzaymah, Muzlaqah ibn Malik ibn Ju'sham, and the Banu Mudlij, who had made a treaty with the Prophet (ﷺ) that they would not fight him nor assist anyone against him.

Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr said: It was revealed concerning Asma' bint Abi Bakr. Her mother Qutaylah bint 'Abd al-'Uzza ibn Asad, of the Banu Malik ibn Hanbal, came to her in Madinah with gifts of dried fruits, cloth and butter, while she was a polytheist. Asma' said: "I will not accept a gift from you, nor will you enter my house, until I ask permission of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." 'A'ishah said to her: "[Ask] the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded her to let her mother enter her home, accept her gift, honor her and treat her well.

Murrah al-Hamdani and 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi said: It was revealed concerning a group of the Banu Hashim, among them al-'Abbas.

﴿Allah only forbids you from those who fight you over the religion, expel you from your homes, and aid in your expulsion — that you make allies of them. And whoever makes allies of them, those are the wrongdoers﴾ — those who place loyalty in other than its proper place.

﴿O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you as emigrants...﴾ — the verse.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set out intending 'Umrah, until when he reached al-Hudaybiyah, the polytheists of Makkah made a treaty with him: whoever came to him from the people of Makkah, he would return to them; and whoever of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went over to the people of Makkah, that person would belong to them and they would not return him to him. They wrote this as a document and sealed it. Then Subay'ah bint al-Harith al-Aslamiyyah came, a Muslim woman, after the completion of the document, while the Prophet (ﷺ) was at al-Hudaybiyah. Her husband, a traveler from the Banu Makhzum — and Muqatil said he was Safwan ibn al-Rahib — came seeking her, and he was a disbeliever. He said: "O Muhammad, return my wife to me, for you have stipulated for us that you would return to us whoever came to you from us, and this seal of the document is not yet dry." So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, when the believing women come to you as emigrants﴾ — from the abode of disbelief to the abode of Islam.

﴿...so test them.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: Their testing is that he asks them to swear that they did not leave out of hatred for a husband, nor out of aversion to one land in favor of another, nor seeking worldly gain, but only out of love for Allah and His Messenger. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made her swear that she had not left out of hatred for her husband, nor out of desire for a man among us, and that she had only left out of desire for Islam. She swore by Allah, besides whom there is no god, to that effect. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave her dower and what had been spent on her, and did not return her to him. 'Umar then married her. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would return the men who came and would detain the women who came, when they were tested, and he would give their husbands their dowers.

This is His saying, glorified is He: ﴿If you know them to be believers, do not return them to the disbelievers. They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them [the disbelievers]. And give them [the disbelievers, i.e., their husbands] what they have spent [as dower]. And there is no blame upon you for marrying them when you have given them their due compensation [dowers]. And do not hold onto marriage ties with disbelieving women...﴾ — even if they have disbelieving husbands in the abode of disbelief, because Islam has separated them, once their wombs have been cleansed.

﴿And do not hold onto marriage ties with disbelieving women﴾ — the common reading is with the lightened form, from al-Imsak (holding), and the bā' is extra; its meaning: "do not hold to the marriage ties of disbelieving women." Al-Hasan, Abu 'Amr, Ya'qub and Abu Hatim read it with the emphasized form, from al-tamassuk (clinging). They say: "I held onto the thing and clung to it." ʿIṣam is the plural of ʿiṣmah, which is what one holds to of a contract or a tie, and kawāfir is the plural of kāfirah. Allah forbade the believers from remaining in marriage with polytheist women and commanded them to separate from them. Ibn 'Abbas said: He says: do not cling to the marriage ties of disbelieving women from one who had a disbelieving wife in Makkah; she is not to be counted as such, for her tie to him has been severed and she is no longer his wife. And if a Muslim woman from the people of Makkah comes to you, whose husband there is a disbeliever, then do not count him, for his tie to her has been severed.

Al-Zuhri said: When this verse was revealed, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) divorced two wives he had in Makkah who were polytheists: Qurayabah bint Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah, whom Mu'awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan married after him while they were still polytheists in Makkah; and the other, Umm Kulthum bint 'Amr ibn Harwal al-Khuza'iyyah, mother of 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, whom Abu Jahm ibn Hudhayfah ibn Ghanim — a man of her people — married, while they were still polytheists. Talhah ibn 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Uthman ibn 'Amr al-Taymi had Arwa bint Rabi'ah ibn al-Harith ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib as his wife, and Islam separated them when the Qur'an forbade holding onto ties with disbelieving women. Talhah had emigrated while she was in Makkah following her people's religion. Then after Talhah, Khalid ibn Sa'id ibn al-'As ibn Umayyah ibn 'Abd Shams married her in Islam; she was among the women of the disbelievers who fled to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so he detained them and gave her to Khalid in marriage. Umaymah bint Bishr had been married to Thabit ibn al-Dahdahah, and she fled from him — while he was then a disbeliever — to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who married her to Sahl ibn Hunayf, and she bore 'Abdullah ibn Sahl. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 28/92.]]

Al-Sha'bi said: Zaynab, daughter of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), was the wife of Abu al-'As ibn al-Rabi'. She embraced Islam and joined the Prophet (ﷺ) in Madinah, while al-'As remained a polytheist in Makkah. Then he came to Madinah, and Zaynab granted him protection, then he embraced Islam, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) returned her to him.

**Verse 60:11 and its commentary**

"And ask, O believers, for what you spent on your wives who went off to the polytheists, namely their dowries from marriage to them. And let the polytheists ask, after the believers, for what they spent on the believing women who went over to you if they marry one of you." Meaning: what they paid as bridewealth. "That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise." Al-Azhari said:

Had it not been for the covenant and truce that existed between the Prophet ﷺ and the Quraysh on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, he would have retained the women and not returned their dowries to them. He would do the same with those Muslim women who came before the covenant. When this verse was revealed, the believers acknowledged the judgment of Allah, the Exalted, and paid what they had been commanded regarding the expenses of the polytheists on their women. The polytheists, however, refused to acknowledge the judgment of Allah regarding the payment of the expenses of the Muslims. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And if any of your wives have gone over to the disbelievers, and you have a turn (of gains) against them, then give those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent﴾ (60:11). "And if you lose any of your wives to the disbelievers, so that they go over to them as apostates..." (The verb) ﴿fa-'aqabtum﴾ is read by the majority with an alif, and this reading is preferred by Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim. Ibrahim, Humayd, and al-A'raj read ﴿fa-'aqqabtum﴾ with shaddah. Mujahid read ﴿fa-a'qabtum﴾ on the pattern of ﴿af'altum﴾, and said: "You did to them as they did to you." Al-Zuhri read ﴿fa-'aqabtum﴾ without alif and light, and read ﴿fa-'aqibtum﴾ with a kasrah on the qaf and light, and said: "You took spoils."

All of these are dialectal variants with the same meaning. It is said: ʿaqaba, ʿaqqaba, ʿaqaba, ʿaqiba, aʿqaba, yaʿqubu, iʿtaqaba, and taʿaqaba, meaning "to gain (spoil)."

The meaning of the verse: "You fought and obtained from the disbelievers ʿuqba, which is the spoils, and you prevailed, and the outcome was in your favor." Al-Mu'arrikh said: its meaning is "you succeeded them and the affair came into your hands." Al-Farra' said: ʿaqqaba and ʿaqaba are like taṣʿara and taṣaʿʿara. It was also said: "one raid after another."

﴿So give those whose wives had gone to the disbelievers among you the equivalent of what they had spent﴾ on them, from the spoils that came into your hands from the property of the disbelievers. It was also said: "fa-ʿaqabtum" means "you executed the apostate woman," i.e., you killed her.

All the believing women of the emigrants who went over to the polytheists and reverted from Islam numbered six women: Umm al-Hakam bint Abi Sufyan, who was married to ʿIyad ibn Shaddad al-Fihri; Fatimah bint Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah, sister of Umm Salamah, who was married to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab; when ʿUmar wished to emigrate, she refused and apostatized; Yaruʿ bint ʿUqbah, who was married to Shammas ibn ʿUthman; ʿAbdah bint ʿAbd al-ʿUzza ibn Fadlah, whose husband was ʿUmar ibn ʿAbdun; Hind bint Abi Jahl ibn Hisham, who was married to Hisham ibn al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il; and Kulthum bint Jarwal, who was married to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave them their dowries from the spoils. [See Tafsir al-Qurtubi 18/70, and Kitab al-Mujr 433.]

He said: "O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, I have not disbelieved since I embraced Islam, nor have I deceived you since I gave you counsel, nor have I responded to them since I parted from them. Abdullah ibn Hamid related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ishaq related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ghalib related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Samad related to us, saying: Layth related to us, from Abu al-Dunayr, from Jabir, that a slave of Hatib came complaining about Hatib to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Hatib will surely enter the Fire!" Allah, glorified is He, revealed concerning the matter of Hatib and his correspondence with the polytheists: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies, extending to them affection...﴾ — "extending to them affection": here "bi" (with) is extra (ṣilah), like the saying of a speaker: "I want to go" and "I want to go with" — Allah, glorified is He, says: ﴿And whoever intends therein deviation by wrongdoing﴾ [[Surat al-Hajj: 25.]], meaning deviation in wrongdoing. meaning: she drank. [[Jami' al-Bayan of al-Tabari: 28/73.]]

﴿Never will your relatives benefit you or your children on the Day of Resurrection.﴾ He says: Do not let your kinship and your children, who are in Makkah, lead you to betray the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the believers, to abandon giving them counsel, and to take their enemies as allies and support them. **Verse 60:11 and its commentary**

"And ask, O believers, for what you spent on your wives who went off to the polytheists, namely their dowries from marriage to them. And let the polytheists ask, after the believers, for what they spent on the believing women who went over to you if they marry one of you." Meaning: what they paid as bridewealth. "That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise." Al-Azhari said:

Had it not been for the covenant and truce that existed between the Prophet ﷺ and the Quraysh on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, he would have retained the women and not returned their dowries to them. He would do the same with those Muslim women who came before the covenant. When this verse was revealed, the believers acknowledged the judgment of Allah, the Exalted, and paid what they had been commanded regarding the expenses of the polytheists on their women. The polytheists, however, refused to acknowledge the judgment of Allah regarding the payment of the expenses of the Muslims. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And if any of your wives have gone over to the disbelievers, and you have a turn (of gains) against them, then give those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent﴾ (60:11). "And if you lose any of your wives to the disbelievers, so that they go over to them as apostates..." (The verb) ﴿fa-'aqabtum﴾ is read by the majority with an alif, and this reading is preferred by Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim. Ibrahim, Humayd, and al-A'raj read ﴿fa-'aqqabtum﴾ with shaddah. Mujahid read ﴿fa-a'qabtum﴾ on the pattern of ﴿af'altum﴾, and said: "You did to them as they did to you." Al-Zuhri read ﴿fa-'aqabtum﴾ without alif and light, and read ﴿fa-'aqibtum﴾ with a kasrah on the qaf and light, and said: "You took spoils."

All of these are dialectal variants with the same meaning. It is said: ʿaqaba, ʿaqqaba, ʿaqaba, ʿaqiba, aʿqaba, yaʿqubu, iʿtaqaba, and taʿaqaba, meaning "to gain (spoil)."

The meaning of the verse: "You fought and obtained from the disbelievers ʿuqba, which is the spoils, and you prevailed, and the outcome was in your favor." Al-Mu'arrikh said: its meaning is "you succeeded them and the affair came into your hands." Al-Farra' said: ʿaqqaba and ʿaqaba are like taṣʿara and taṣaʿʿara. It was also said: "one raid after another."

﴿So give those whose wives had gone to the disbelievers among you the equivalent of what they had spent﴾ on them, from the spoils that came into your hands from the property of the disbelievers. It was also said: "fa-ʿaqabtum" means "you executed the apostate woman," i.e., you killed her.

All the believing women of the emigrants who went over to the polytheists and reverted from Islam numbered six women: Umm al-Hakam bint Abi Sufyan, who was married to ʿIyad ibn Shaddad al-Fihri; Fatimah bint Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah, sister of Umm Salamah, who was married to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab; when ʿUmar wished to emigrate, she refused and apostatized; Yaruʿ bint ʿUqbah, who was married to Shammas ibn ʿUthman; ʿAbdah bint ʿAbd al-ʿUzza ibn Fadlah, whose husband was ʿUmar ibn ʿAbdun; Hind bint Abi Jahl ibn Hisham, who was married to Hisham ibn al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il; and Kulthum bint Jarwal, who was married to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave them their dowries from the spoils. [See Tafsir al-Qurtubi 18/70, and Kitab al-Mujr 433.]

**Verse 60:11 and its commentary**

"And ask, O believers, for what you spent on your wives who went off to the polytheists, namely their dowries from marriage to them. And let the polytheists ask, after the believers, for what they spent on the believing women who went over to you if they marry one of you." Meaning: what they paid as bridewealth. "That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise." Al-Azhari said:

Had it not been for the covenant and truce that existed between the Prophet ﷺ and the Quraysh on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, he would have retained the women and not returned their dowries to them. He would do the same with those Muslim women who came before the covenant. When this verse was revealed, the believers acknowledged the judgment of Allah, the Exalted, and paid what they had been commanded regarding the expenses of the polytheists on their women. The polytheists, however, refused to acknowledge the judgment of Allah regarding the payment of the expenses of the Muslims. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And if any of your wives have gone over to the disbelievers, and you have a turn (of gains) against them, then give those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent﴾ (60:11). "And if you lose any of your wives to the disbelievers, so that they go over to them as apostates..." (The verb) ﴿fa-'aqabtum﴾ is read by the majority with an alif, and this reading is preferred by Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim. Ibrahim, Humayd, and al-A'raj read ﴿fa-'aqqabtum﴾ with shaddah. Mujahid read ﴿fa-a'qabtum﴾ on the pattern of ﴿af'altum﴾, and said: "You did to them as they did to you." Al-Zuhri read ﴿fa-'aqabtum﴾ without alif and light, and read ﴿fa-'aqibtum﴾ with a kasrah on the qaf and light, and said: "You took spoils."

All of these are dialectal variants with the same meaning. It is said: ʿaqaba, ʿaqqaba, ʿaqaba, ʿaqiba, aʿqaba, yaʿqubu, iʿtaqaba, and taʿaqaba, meaning "to gain (spoil)."

The meaning of the verse: "You fought and obtained from the disbelievers ʿuqba, which is the spoils, and you prevailed, and the outcome was in your favor." Al-Mu'arrikh said: its meaning is "you succeeded them and the affair came into your hands." Al-Farra' said: ʿaqqaba and ʿaqaba are like taṣʿara and taṣaʿʿara. It was also said: "one raid after another."

﴿So give those whose wives had gone to the disbelievers among you the equivalent of what they had spent﴾ on them, from the spoils that came into your hands from the property of the disbelievers. It was also said: "fa-ʿaqabtum" means "you executed the apostate woman," i.e., you killed her.

All the believing women of the emigrants who went over to the polytheists and reverted from Islam numbered six women: Umm al-Hakam bint Abi Sufyan, who was married to ʿIyad ibn Shaddad al-Fihri; Fatimah bint Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah, sister of Umm Salamah, who was married to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab; when ʿUmar wished to emigrate, she refused and apostatized; Yaruʿ bint ʿUqbah, who was married to Shammas ibn ʿUthman; ʿAbdah bint ʿAbd al-ʿUzza ibn Fadlah, whose husband was ʿUmar ibn ʿAbdun; Hind bint Abi Jahl ibn Hisham, who was married to Hisham ibn al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il; and Kulthum bint Jarwal, who was married to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave them their dowries from the spoils. [See Tafsir al-Qurtubi 18/70, and Kitab al-Mujr 433.]

**Verse 60:11 and its commentary**

"And ask, O believers, for what you spent on your wives who went off to the polytheists, namely their dowries from marriage to them. And let the polytheists ask, after the believers, for what they spent on the believing women who went over to you if they marry one of you." Meaning: what they paid as bridewealth. "That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise." Al-Azhari said:

Had it not been for the covenant and truce that existed between the Prophet ﷺ and the Quraysh on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, he would have retained the women and not returned their dowries to them. He would do the same with those Muslim women who came before the covenant. When this verse was revealed, the believers acknowledged the judgment of Allah, the Exalted, and paid what they had been commanded regarding the expenses of the polytheists on their women. The polytheists, however, refused to acknowledge the judgment of Allah regarding the payment of the expenses of the Muslims. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And if any of your wives have gone over to the disbelievers, and you have a turn (of gains) against them, then give those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent﴾ (60:11). "And if you lose any of your wives to the disbelievers, so that they go over to them as apostates..." (The verb) ﴿fa-'aqabtum﴾ is read by the majority with an alif, and this reading is preferred by Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim. Ibrahim, Humayd, and al-A'raj read ﴿fa-'aqqabtum﴾ with shaddah. Mujahid read ﴿fa-a'qabtum﴾ on the pattern of ﴿af'altum﴾, and said: "You did to them as they did to you." Al-Zuhri read ﴿fa-'aqabtum﴾ without alif and light, and read ﴿fa-'aqibtum﴾ with a kasrah on the qaf and light, and said: "You took spoils."

All of these are dialectal variants with the same meaning. It is said: ʿaqaba, ʿaqqaba, ʿaqaba, ʿaqiba, aʿqaba, yaʿqubu, iʿtaqaba, and taʿaqaba, meaning "to gain (spoil)."

The meaning of the verse: "You fought and obtained from the disbelievers ʿuqba, which is the spoils, and you prevailed, and the outcome was in your favor." Al-Mu'arrikh said: its meaning is "you succeeded them and the affair came into your hands." Al-Farra' said: ʿaqqaba and ʿaqaba are like taṣʿara and taṣaʿʿara. It was also said: "one raid after another."

﴿So give those whose wives had gone to the disbelievers among you the equivalent of what they had spent﴾ on them, from the spoils that came into your hands from the property of the disbelievers. It was also said: "fa-ʿaqabtum" means "you executed the apostate woman," i.e., you killed her.

All the believing women of the emigrants who went over to the polytheists and reverted from Islam numbered six women: Umm al-Hakam bint Abi Sufyan, who was married to ʿIyad ibn Shaddad al-Fihri; Fatimah bint Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah, sister of Umm Salamah, who was married to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab; when ʿUmar wished to emigrate, she refused and apostatized; Yaruʿ bint ʿUqbah, who was married to Shammas ibn ʿUthman; ʿAbdah bint ʿAbd al-ʿUzza ibn Fadlah, whose husband was ʿUmar ibn ʿAbdun; Hind bint Abi Jahl ibn Hisham, who was married to Hisham ibn al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il; and Kulthum bint Jarwal, who was married to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave them their dowries from the spoils. [See Tafsir al-Qurtubi 18/70, and Kitab al-Mujr 433.]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy as allies...﴾

They said: and he clothed her in a cloak, so that she might deliver the letter to the people of Makkah. He wrote in the letter: "From Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah to the people of Makkah: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intends you, so take your precautions." "And ask, O believers, for what you spent on your wives who went off to the polytheists, namely their dowries from marriage to them. And let the polytheists ask, after the believers, for what they spent on the believing women who went over to you if they marry one of you." Meaning: what they paid as bridewealth. Had it not been for the covenant and truce that existed between the Prophet ﷺ and the Quraysh on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, he would have retained the women and not returned their dowries to them. He would do the same with those Muslim women who came before the covenant. When this verse was revealed, the believers acknowledged the judgment of Allah, the Exalted, and paid what they had been commanded regarding the expenses of the polytheists on their women. The polytheists, however, refused to acknowledge the judgment of Allah regarding the payment of the expenses of the Muslims. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And if any of your wives have gone over to the disbelievers, and you have a turn (of gains) against them, then give those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent﴾ (60:11). **Verse 60:11 and its commentary**

"And ask, O believers, for what you spent on your wives who went off to the polytheists, namely their dowries from marriage to them. And let the polytheists ask, after the believers, for what they spent on the believing women who went over to you if they marry one of you." Meaning: what they paid as bridewealth. "That is the judgment of Allah; He judges between you, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise." Al-Azhari said:

Had it not been for the covenant and truce that existed between the Prophet ﷺ and the Quraysh on the day of al-Hudaybiyah, he would have retained the women and not returned their dowries to them. He would do the same with those Muslim women who came before the covenant. When this verse was revealed, the believers acknowledged the judgment of Allah, the Exalted, and paid what they had been commanded regarding the expenses of the polytheists on their women. The polytheists, however, refused to acknowledge the judgment of Allah regarding the payment of the expenses of the Muslims. So Allah, the Exalted, revealed: ﴿And if any of your wives have gone over to the disbelievers, and you have a turn (of gains) against them, then give those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they had spent﴾ (60:11). "And if you lose any of your wives to the disbelievers, so that they go over to them as apostates..." (The verb) ﴿fa-'aqabtum﴾ is read by the majority with an alif, and this reading is preferred by Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim. Ibrahim, Humayd, and al-A'raj read ﴿fa-'aqqabtum﴾ with shaddah. Mujahid read ﴿fa-a'qabtum﴾ on the pattern of ﴿af'altum﴾, and said: "You did to them as they did to you." Al-Zuhri read ﴿fa-'aqabtum﴾ without alif and light, and read ﴿fa-'aqibtum﴾ with a kasrah on the qaf and light, and said: "You took spoils."

All of these are dialectal variants with the same meaning. It is said: ʿaqaba, ʿaqqaba, ʿaqaba, ʿaqiba, aʿqaba, yaʿqubu, iʿtaqaba, and taʿaqaba, meaning "to gain (spoil)."

The meaning of the verse: "You fought and obtained from the disbelievers ʿuqba, which is the spoils, and you prevailed, and the outcome was in your favor." Al-Mu'arrikh said: its meaning is "you succeeded them and the affair came into your hands." Al-Farra' said: ʿaqqaba and ʿaqaba are like taṣʿara and taṣaʿʿara. It was also said: "one raid after another."

﴿So give those whose wives had gone to the disbelievers among you the equivalent of what they had spent﴾ on them, from the spoils that came into your hands from the property of the disbelievers. It was also said: "fa-ʿaqabtum" means "you executed the apostate woman," i.e., you killed her.

All the believing women of the emigrants who went over to the polytheists and reverted from Islam numbered six women: Umm al-Hakam bint Abi Sufyan, who was married to ʿIyad ibn Shaddad al-Fihri; Fatimah bint Abi Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah, sister of Umm Salamah, who was married to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab; when ʿUmar wished to emigrate, she refused and apostatized; Yaruʿ bint ʿUqbah, who was married to Shammas ibn ʿUthman; ʿAbdah bint ʿAbd al-ʿUzza ibn Fadlah, whose husband was ʿUmar ibn ʿAbdun; Hind bint Abi Jahl ibn Hisham, who was married to Hisham ibn al-ʿAs ibn Wa'il; and Kulthum bint Jarwal, who was married to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave them their dowries from the spoils. [See Tafsir al-Qurtubi 18/70, and Kitab al-Mujr 433.]

﴿And fear Allah, in whom you believe.﴾

O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you... (Qur'an 60:12), the rest of the verse.

That was on the day of the conquest of Makkah. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished taking the pledge of the men, he was on al-Safa, and 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was below him, taking the pledge of the women on the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) command and conveying it to them. Hind bint 'Utbah, the wife of Abu Sufyan, was veiled and disguised among the women, fearing that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would recognize her. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I take your pledge that you will not associate anything with Allah." Hind raised her head and said, "By Allah, you are demanding of us a thing that we have not seen you demand of the men." He took the pledge of the men that day only for Islam and jihad. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "And that they will not steal." Hind said, "Abu Sufyan is a stingy man, and I take some of his wealth, a few things, and I do not know whether it is lawful for me or not." Abu Sufyan said, "Whatever you have taken in the past and whatever you take in the future is lawful for you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed, recognized her, and said to her: "And you are indeed Hind bint 'Utbah?" She said, "Yes. So pardon what has passed, O Prophet of Allah; may Allah pardon you." He said: "And that they will not commit adultery." Hind said, "Does a free woman commit adultery?" He said: "And that they will not kill their children..." Hind said, "We raised them when they were small, and you killed them when they were grown; you and they know best." Her son Handhalah ibn Abi Sufyan had been killed on the day of Badr. 'Umar laughed until he fell onto his back, and the Prophet (ﷺ) smiled. He said: "And that they will not bring a slander which they have fabricated between their hands and their feet..." This means that a woman attributes to her husband a child that is not his. Hind said, "By Allah, slander is ugly, and he only commands us to noble character." "And that they will not disobey you in what is right..." She said, "We did not sit in this gathering of ours while having in our hearts any intention to disobey you in anything." So the women affirmed what had been taken from them. [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/456.]]

The scholars differed about the manner in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the pledge from the women.

We were told by Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hamdun, who said: Makki informed us, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr informed us, who said: Sufyan informed us. And 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, who said: Bishr ibn Mutar informed us, who said: Sufyan ibn 'Utbah informed us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, that he heard Umaymah bint Ruqaiqah say: "I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) along with a group of women. He said: 'In what you are able and capable of.' I said: 'The Messenger of Allah is more merciful to us than we are to ourselves.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, shake our hands.' He said: 'I do not shake hands with women. My saying to one woman is like my saying to a hundred women.'" [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/357.]]

And Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hamdun informed us, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya informed us, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to take the pledge of the women by speech, with this verse: ﴿that they will not associate anything with Allah﴾." She said: "The hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never touched the hand of a woman, except the hand of a woman he owned."

Al-Sa'ri said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) used to take the pledge of the women while he had a cloth of wool over his hand."

'Amr ibn Shu'ayb narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that the Prophet (ﷺ), when he took the pledge of the women, called for a vessel of water, dipped his hand in it, and then the women dipped their hands in it.

Al-Kalbi said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would stipulate conditions to the women, and 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) would shake their hands."

The exegetes differed about the meaning of "what is right" (al-ma'ruf). Al-Qurazi said: "What is right is that in which they do not disobey him." Rabi' said: "Everything that agrees with the obedience of Allah is right. Allah did not want His Prophet to be obeyed in disobedience of Allah." Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Madani said: "They do not disobey you in every matter in which there is their guidance." Mujahid said: "A woman should not be alone with men." Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: "They should not shave their heads, nor tear their clothes, nor burn a garment, nor pull out their hair, nor scratch a face, nor loosen their hair, nor speak to men except one with a mahram (a close male relative they may not marry), nor be alone with a man who is not a mahram, nor travel for three days with someone who is not a mahram." O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you... (Qur'an 60:12), the rest of the verse.

That was on the day of the conquest of Makkah. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished taking the pledge of the men, he was on al-Safa, and 'Umar ibn al-Khattab was below him, taking the pledge of the women on the Messenger of Allah's (ﷺ) command and conveying it to them. Hind bint 'Utbah, the wife of Abu Sufyan, was veiled and disguised among the women, fearing that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would recognize her. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "I take your pledge that you will not associate anything with Allah." Hind raised her head and said, "By Allah, you are demanding of us a thing that we have not seen you demand of the men." He took the pledge of the men that day only for Islam and jihad. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "And that they will not steal." Hind said, "Abu Sufyan is a stingy man, and I take some of his wealth, a few things, and I do not know whether it is lawful for me or not." Abu Sufyan said, "Whatever you have taken in the past and whatever you take in the future is lawful for you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed, recognized her, and said to her: "And you are indeed Hind bint 'Utbah?" She said, "Yes. So pardon what has passed, O Prophet of Allah; may Allah pardon you." He said: "And that they will not commit adultery." Hind said, "Does a free woman commit adultery?" He said: "And that they will not kill their children..." Hind said, "We raised them when they were small, and you killed them when they were grown; you and they know best." Her son Handhalah ibn Abi Sufyan had been killed on the day of Badr. 'Umar laughed until he fell onto his back, and the Prophet (ﷺ) smiled. He said: "And that they will not bring a slander which they have fabricated between their hands and their feet..." This means that a woman attributes to her husband a child that is not his. Hind said, "By Allah, slander is ugly, and he only commands us to noble character." "And that they will not disobey you in what is right..." She said, "We did not sit in this gathering of ours while having in our hearts any intention to disobey you in anything." So the women affirmed what had been taken from them. [[Tafsir Majma' al-Bayan: 9/456.]]

The scholars differed about the manner in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) took the pledge from the women.

We were told by Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hamdun, who said: Makki informed us, who said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Bishr informed us, who said: Sufyan informed us. And 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, who said: Bishr ibn Mutar informed us, who said: Sufyan ibn 'Utbah informed us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, that he heard Umaymah bint Ruqaiqah say: "I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) along with a group of women. He said: 'In what you are able and capable of.' I said: 'The Messenger of Allah is more merciful to us than we are to ourselves.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, shake our hands.' He said: 'I do not shake hands with women. My saying to one woman is like my saying to a hundred women.'" [[Musnad Ahmad: 6/357.]]

And Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Hamdun informed us, who said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan informed us, who said: Muhammad ibn Yahya informed us, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to take the pledge of the women by speech, with this verse: ﴿that they will not associate anything with Allah﴾." She said: "The hand of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never touched the hand of a woman, except the hand of a woman he owned."

Al-Sa'ri said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) used to take the pledge of the women while he had a cloth of wool over his hand."

'Amr ibn Shu'ayb narrated from his father, from his grandfather, that the Prophet (ﷺ), when he took the pledge of the women, called for a vessel of water, dipped his hand in it, and then the women dipped their hands in it.

Al-Kalbi said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would stipulate conditions to the women, and 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) would shake their hands."

The exegetes differed about the meaning of "what is right" (al-ma'ruf). Al-Qurazi said: "What is right is that in which they do not disobey him." Rabi' said: "Everything that agrees with the obedience of Allah is right. Allah did not want His Prophet to be obeyed in disobedience of Allah." Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah al-Madani said: "They do not disobey you in every matter in which there is their guidance." Mujahid said: "A woman should not be alone with men." Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Muhammad ibn al-Sa'ib and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: "They should not shave their heads, nor tear their clothes, nor burn a garment, nor pull out their hair, nor scratch a face, nor loosen their hair, nor speak to men except one with a mahram (a close male relative they may not marry), nor be alone with a man who is not a mahram, nor travel for three days with someone who is not a mahram." Ibn 'Abbas said: "They should not wail."
